parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, and this state/province currently imposes no restroom restriction (two cities protect it; the pending facilities bill is not law), with a hate-crimes law covering gender identity — real positives that keep it out of the 0.35–0.45 tier. The heaviest visitor-facing exposure is at entry: national screening flags document sex discrepancies, allows refusal for reasonable doubt about sex, and contemplates a lifetime fraud finding; foreign governments issued advisories and neighbours' citizens were detained over visa issues. Discovery probability is therefore state-engineered for anyone whose papers are imperfect. If detained, national immigration-custody and corrections practice is documented as abusive (forced labour, beatings, sexual violence, care denial) with no visitor remedy. Marker bans, care bans and employment gaps are resident-facing and not deducted. Elevated Risk: known border exposure plus severe custody downside, but no universal facility or custody-placement rule here.
